question.text: In a BULLET FI strategy, portfolio duration is concentrated at ONE maturity point. Compared to a BARBELL with equal duration, which has HIGHER convexity?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook constructs the barbell as roughly 40% short-term, 40% long-term and 20% mid-term bonds, dispersing maturities at both ends of the curve. It also says portfolio convexity can be changed by shifting the maturity/duration distribution, and that a positive-convexity bond has a higher expected return than an identical-duration lower-convexity bond when rates change. The barbell's dispersed maturity profile is therefore directionally consistent with higher convexity than a single-maturity bullet of similar duration. The Trap: Same-duration portfolios do not necessarily have the same convexity, because dispersion of cash flows across the curve matters. Duration alone does not determine convexity. Note: Pages 343-345 cover barbell construction, the maturity/duration drivers of convexity, and the return advantage of higher-convexity bonds at equal duration.
